answer.rationale: memory_c2 shows a prior successful switch to a low-cost vendor with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing; memory_c4 shows that even when staying with an incumbent, benchmarking against market rates forced concessions on price and terms. The incumbent has refused to reopen price, and the low-cost vendor's quote alone meets the 18% mandate. Switching primary supply is the only single action that satisfies the cost mandate and delivery continuity (14-day window, no auto-renew). Adding a second source (memory_c3) is prudent but cannot, by itself, meet the 18% cut if the incumbent price is unchanged; it will be queued for next cycle. The 94% assembly-line load with no buffer is the key risk: the switch must include a confirmed delivery schedule and a 14-day overlap/transition window to prevent a gap. I am requesting verification of memory_c2 (to confirm onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy held in the original record) and memory_c4 (to confirm the benchmarking leverage was real and not a one-off concession), before final commitment.
